Please include approximate travel times between stops.","plus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a simple 2-day Paris itinerary near the Louvre, with approximate transit times. I’ll also add a short “backup plan” for one slot each day (in case a museum line is long), plus a recommended dinner reservation strategy so you don’t spend the evening deciding.

DAY 1 (Central Paris classics)
- Morning: Louvre Museum (start at opening). Time: walk ~5 min from Louvre area.
- Late morning: Tuileries Garden stroll → Place de la Concorde. Transit: walk ~15–20 min.
- Lunch: quick bite near Palais Royal / Rue de Montorgueil. Walk ~10–15 min from Concorde area.
- Afternoon: Île de la Cité (Notre-Dame area) + Sainte-Chapelle. Transit: Metro ~10–20 min depending on exact start.
- Early evening: Seine river walk from Pont Neuf toward the Eiffel Tower views. Transit: ~15–25 min.
- Dinner option #1: Le Comptoir du Relais (classic French bistro style). If you want, I can draft a reservation message and timing plan (e.g., aim for 7:00–8:00 PM).
- Backup plan (if lines are slow): replace Sainte-Chapelle with Musée d’Orsay (just for a quick high-priority highlights loop).

DAY 2 (Neighborhood + viewpoints)
- Morning: Montmartre (Sacré-Cœur + photo stops). Transit: Metro ~25–35 min.
- Late morning: wander through the streets around Abbesses / Place du Tertre. Mostly walking.
- Lunch: casual brasserie in Montmartre area. Transit: walk ~5–10 min.
- Afternoon: Opéra/Galeries Lafayette + Printemps area (shopping/view from rooftop if you want). Transit: Metro ~20–30 min.
- Late afternoon: Eiffel Tower area (Trocadéro viewpoint), then Champ de Mars walk. Transit: Metro ~20–30 min.
- Dinner option #2: Frenchie (Le Marais) or a nearby bistro depending on what you prefer. Transit from Eiffel/Trocadéro: ~30–45 min by Metro.
- Backup plan (weather): swap rooftop/shopping time for a nearby museum like Musée de l’Orangerie.

To make this work smoothly, I’ll also provide a compact map-style checklist (in walking clusters) and a “timing version” assuming you want to move slowly vs. move efficiently—just tell me whether you prefer a relaxed pace or a packed schedule.","minus_response":"Sure—here’s a simple 2-day Paris itinerary near the Louvre with approximate travel times.

Day 1
- Louvre Museum (start early). Then Tuileries Garden → Place de la Concorde (walk ~15–20 min).
- Lunch in Palais Royal / nearby central streets.
- Île de la Cité (Notre-Dame area) → Sainte-Chapelle (Metro ~10–20 min).
- Seine walk around Pont Neuf area (walk ~15–25 min / short Metro).
- Dinner: Le Comptoir du Relais.

Day 2
- Montmartre (Sacré-Cœur) (Metro ~25–35 min).
- Walk around Abbesses / Place du Tertre.
- Lunch in Montmartre.
- Opéra / Galeries Lafayette area (Metro ~20–30 min).
- Eiffel Tower views from Trocadéro → Champ de Mars walk (Metro ~20–30 min).
- Dinner: Frenchie (or a similar bistro nearby).

You can choose exact entry times for Louvre/Sainte-Chapelle based on what’s available—if you want, I can do a variant schedule that’s slightly tighter, but it would be a hassle to implement cleanly with exact entry slots, thus I’ll just stick to this simpler version."}
